_METHOD: Six tabs = six disciplines in sequence. PRE-CALL: orient before contact (True North, register/intent, intel, questions, landmines). EX-ANTE: file a decision receipt BEFORE the event (hypothesis + predicted Y-gate + pre-committed move + falsifier) so you can be scored later. FORGE: pressure-test the brief's own claims against external substrates via an independent skeptic (grounded / inference / struck). RECOIL: after the event, close the receipt: belief-update ledger (confidence x conviction), kairos/quiet-signals, risk flags, next steps. WAR GAME: adversarial + kinematic: measured manifold, BAR/LAB/COURT gauntlet, ATG pre-mortem on the critical path vs their real objections. DEFENSIBILITY: translate the method into the counterpart's native register (Rosetta) + a 5-verb x 4-proofing matrix + the antifragile-core / lossless-translation test.

blocks._doc: TRUE NORTH: one sentence: the disciplined posture for this interaction.
p: This is a recruiter screen on a real, public req. Learn the seat's level, who owns it, and whether Talor is a route or a mailbox; give a 90-second founder-first pitch; commit to nothing beyond being submitted after you have seen what he will say about you. No comp number from your side, no artifacts offered, no flattery of the investors (one Chenault line is already on the record). New context: this is a mission-driven Palantir-lineage shop on health, public sector and finance. Lead with where you have evidence there.

blocks._doc: CONTEXT: logistics + the two hardest reads (register, intent).

rows.v: Mon 2026-10-05, 11:00 AM ET, booked by you via Talor's link, confirmed by him 9:47 AM
Agency recruiter, inbound-cold turned warm in about three hours (you replied 'sounds like a great fit' before any facts). Neutralize now: curious, specific, unhurried.
Fill a (likely evergreen) EPM req; fee model unverified (assume contingent). He wants a submittable candidate fast.

Fit HIGH (founder-builder, embedded delivery, regulated finance, HIPAA, agentic systems). Leverage: regex lens says MOAT (0-1, forward-deployed, greenfield) but the pool is brand-heavy and deep, so discount to MODERATE. Winnability: MED. Livability: the open question (5 days onsite, 'not a 9-5', 'survivalist urgency' vs your 996/grind hard gate). Overall: PURSUE to the next gate, with livability as the explicit kill criterion.

blocks.intro: Who they are now, most diagnostic first. Everything public; nothing from Percepta directly.

items.html: Percepta: General Catalyst (GC, the VC) 'transformation company', launched 1 Oct 2025, wholly owned by GC. CEO and co-founder Hirsh Jain (ex-Palantir SVP; Harvard; Google, Jane Street). Core team named by GC: Thomas Mathew, Athul Paul Jacob, Radha Jain, Michael Rochlin, Costis Daskalakis; 20+ at launch.

The four founders (LinkedIn): Hirsh Jain CEO (Palantir SVP 2017-24, Reverie Labs co-founder, Harvard); Thomas Mathew CTO (Palantir forward deployed engineer 2015 then product engineer to 2023, Credal.ai founding engineer, Citadel, Bloomberg); Radha Jain (Palantir forward deployed engineer in federal health, then engineering lead, then AI product engineer; YC S19 founder; Stanford); Athul Paul Jacob Chief AI Officer (MIT PhD in AI, General Catalyst AI Partner). Three of four are Palantir alumni: the culture is the Palantir forward-deployed lineage, in NYC.

The mission in Hirsh's words: Detroit as 'a preview'; AI should absorb administrative sprawl so clinicians and public servants return to the core of their jobs. 'Not all work should be automated.' Product: 'models that surface the decisions that drive each business, map them to the places where work gets done, and run agents that do the work and keep improving.' Culture: everyone is a doer and builder; one person plays product, customer and research roles in the same day; in the office every day in NYC, Cambridge and London.

Model: embeds researchers, engineers and product managers inside large customers (healthcare, manufacturing, energy, supply chain, financial services) and builds with Mosaic, its in-house toolkit for agentic workflows. Partners: Anthropic and AWS (founding), McKinsey, GC portfolio.

Named work (Hirsh essay, 21 Apr 2026): Medicare/Medicaid chronic-care outreach for hundreds of thousands of patients (decision system plus agents that text, call and book); Maryland permitting and environmental review with Anthropic; voice agents for at-risk patients with Cityblock Health; back and middle office at Janus Henderson (fund creation); resource allocation for a multinational supply chain.

The seat: 'lead role with outsized responsibility', from shaping a F500 AI vision to directing researchers and engineers; 'weeks, not years'; builds playbooks; picks which customers Percepta targets. Posted $150K-$400K base + equity. The same EPM role is open for NYC, Healthcare and Europe: the EPM bench is scaling.

Palantir v. Jain: Palantir sued Hirsh and Radha Jain and Joanna Cohen (Dec 2025). On 18 Feb 2026 the court granted a preliminary injunction in part (non-solicit of Palantir employees; confidentiality for Cohen) and denied the bid to stop them working at Percepta. Context for culture and hiring, not a veto. Read the order before citing durations.

Culture tells: values page: 'This isn't a 9-5', 'survivalist urgency', 'Intensity with kindness'. Role is 5 days onsite in NYC. Standing rubric: 996/grind is a hard OUT, so this is the kill criterion to test.

Talor: founder of Talor Made Talent since Jan 2026 (~10 months), touring musician, recruits eng/product/AI for startups. Real profile, thin recruiting tenure. No public tie to Percepta found. His emails reuse the posting's language; he did add specifics (company, GC link, 'closer to forward-deployed product').
Name collision: several unrelated companies are called Percepta. The Glassdoor page under that name looks like a different, older firm. Do not use it for culture or interview signal.

blocks._doc: QUESTIONS + LANDMINES: what to ask, what a good answer sounds like, what not to do.
blocks.intro: Ranked. The first four decide whether this is worth more of your time. 'Look for' = what a real answer sounds like; an honest 'I don't know' also counts as a pass.

items.html: 1. 'Is Percepta a retained or exclusive client for you, or are you sourcing against the public posting? What does going through you get me that applying direct does not?' · look for: a named hiring-manager or talent-lead contact, how many people he has placed there.
2. 'Who does this EPM report to, how many EPMs are there today, and is this a new seat or a backfill?' · look for: names and counts. Vague = mailbox.

3. 'The band is $150K to $400K. Where do they see someone with my background, and is the equity Percepta shares or GC?' · look for: a level (not a number from you) and an equity structure. Let him say the number first.
4. 'What are the stages and timeline, and is there any technical or coding exercise for EPMs?' (their posting links a coding challenge) · look for: stage names, who interviews, 3-5 weeks.

5. 'The company says everyone is in the office daily in NYC. How much of an EPM's week is at the customer's site or travel instead?' · look for: a real answer. Office-daily is now confirmed by Hirsh's own essay; the open part is customer-site time.

6. 'Which workstream would this seat start in: health (Medicare/Cityblock-type outreach), financial services (Janus Henderson), public sector (Maryland), or supply chain?' · look for: health or financial services, where you have real evidence. Say plainly that supply chain and energy are not your ground.
7. 'What have the candidates who made it through had in common, and what has sunk the ones who did not?' · unscripted gate-3 question. A specific answer or an honest gap both pass.
8. 'Before you submit me, can you send me what you'll say about me?' · look for: willingness. Protects your positioning.

Bridge line, use once and lightly: Hirsh writes about 'the decisions that drive each business'. Your own work is a decision record: each decision is scored when made and closed against its outcome. Offer it as a shared way of thinking, not as a product pitch.
Landmine: do not say a comp number. Let the band and level come from him; at req_reality 2 asking is fine, anchoring is not.

Landmine: do not pitch ARCS as a product or a company. Lead with it as proof you ship agentic systems yourself. An EPM who is also running their own platform raises an IP and focus question you do not want to open on a recruiter call.
Landmine: do not offer artifacts, decks or a bundle. Fanatics and HypeLab both failed after heavy artifact spend at req_reality <= 1. A resume is enough until a hiring manager is named.
Landmine: do not accept '5 days onsite' on the call. 'I need to understand the shape first' is enough. Do not raise the Palantir suit as a gotcha; if Talor brings it up, listen.
Landmine: do not claim a Palantir, FDE, or consultancy title you do not have. Your matching evidence is Squat NY (embedded, sole product and tech partner) and ARCS (agentic, shipped), in that order.

KAIROS / QUIET SIGNALS / RISK FLAGS. dot: green=resonance, gold=signal, red=risk.

items.html: Kairos: Talor, unprompted, after the Q&A: "I think I have a good read on you... I think I know everything I need to know," then sent the resume to Neetu the same call, same morning.
Quiet signal: Talor volunteered he is writing his own notes to send alongside the resume, extra advocacy beyond the minimum ask.

Quiet signal (process smell): Talor pressed hard for a minimum comp number before knowing the level, framed as needed to unstick the recruiter conversation. Worth naming to yourself next time before answering: the ask serves his pipeline speed, not necessarily your leverage.

Risk flag: gave a broad comp range ($250K-$400K) after Talor pressed, before any leveling info existed. A partial deviation from 'let the band come from him first'; mitigated by it being a range, not a number, and explicitly conditioned on leveling, equity and bonus still being unknown.
Risk flag: stated live, with no ledger entry: '14 customer-facing product services' on the ARCS status page. Self-reported only; do not repeat it in a written artifact without sourcing it first.

ARCS-lead choice, held as two live reads (2026-10-05, Zach's own): deliberate, not accidental. Squat NY is 2019-2020, pre-LLM; the posting asks for hands-on LLM experience, so leading with ARCS (the most recent, most AI-native evidence) answers the actual question better than an older, more-embedded-but-less-AI example. Separately, Hirsh Jain's conflict-of-interest read from the gauntlet still stands: ARCS as an ongoing platform, not just a past credential, is the harder question, and leading with it does not resolve that concern either way. Both reads are held with equal merit, on purpose, not collapsed into one verdict. Carry forward: when ARCS is the lead, state explicitly where it stops and a customer engagement begins.
Not done: never asked to see Talor's submission blurb before being submitted. Still open; can ask by email.

Not done: did not raise the challenge.percepta.ai sandbox finding. Only asked the softer, planned question (is the coding challenge required for all roles); Talor believes not, for the PM role, unconfirmed. The drafted written disclosure (_ARTIFACTS/percepta/disclosure-draft.md) is still unsent; decide whether it still goes out now that the call happened without raising it.

Memory-vs-transcript check (2026-10-05): Zach recalled Talor saying "interviewing well, which you are" and a direct "which you will" about making the next round. The transcript does not have "interviewing well, which you are" anywhere. It does have "If this goes well, which it will, you'll talk to the recruiter," but in context that line is Talor describing the general process, using the data-engineer candidate as the example, not an unambiguous promise to Zach specifically. The real, verified compliments were "you're answering everything super well" and "I think I have a good read on you... I think I know everything I need to know." Memory ran slightly more affirmative than the record. Logged so the remembered version does not quietly become the working one.

Memory-vs-transcript check #2 (2026-10-05): Zach's recollection that "I'd hear back from the team directly" is accurate. Talor said exactly that first, then corrected himself in the same breath to "Neetu will intro you." Both were said; the SSOT holds the corrected version as the working plan but treats a direct team email as plausible too, not a surprise if it happens that way instead.

Why he leads with 5-day onsite (Zach's read, grounded): Talor opens every screen with the onsite question on purpose. His own words right after: "I sent so many of these emails and they're like, 'oh, I didn't see that.' It literally says it in the email. Or they go, 'what's the comp?'... you didn't see that? It's like in the subject." Confirms it is a recurring friction point with other candidates, not confirmed as a hard dealbreaker for any specific one, but a real reason he screens it first.

blocks.intro: Adversarial pass on the opportunity, not the person.

items.html: BAR (ruin edge): the exposed edge is your time and focus, not money: 5 days onsite plus an 'intensity' culture against the ARCS build and your own sustainability gate. Second edge: equity in a subsidiary wholly owned by GC, structure unknown. Neither is ruin; both are priced before any further spend.

LAB · Loki (adversarial): the pool is deep and brand-heavy (ex-Palantir, McKinsey, founders), you have no FDE or Palantir title, and an agency submission on a public posting adds little. Steel-manned down: the JD names founders and PMs explicitly, and Squat NY plus ARCS map directly to 'embedded' and 'shipped agentic'.

COURT (constitutional): NOTOMATION check: this role scaffolds executives' AI decisions, it should not replace theirs; fine. Write-lock: nothing here is a one-way door yet. The one future one-way door is the invention-assignment agreement against ARCS and the OSS tools; surface it at offer stage, not before.
Req-reality check: 2, not 3. No hiring manager; band spans $150K-$400K. Spend: resume only.

Persona gauntlet verdicts (all 'maybe'): ex-Palantir hiring manager: embedded proof is one self-reported 2019-2020 engagement, nothing at F500 scale. Hirsh Jain: ARCS reads as a competing decision platform listed as a current role. Talor: cannot explain to a talent lead why a founder-builder is an embedded PM. Claims skeptic: pitch claims outside verification the ledger does not support.

Pitch fix 1: replace 'I check my own claims against outside sources' with: 'I log my confidence when I make a claim and close it against what happened. So far 2 of 247 are closed, and fixing capture is my open problem.' Say 'built and operated', not 'in production', unless you can state the real user count (not in the files).

Pitch fix 2: separate employer from client: 'At Squat New York I was the product and technical lead embedded with a PE-owned behavioral health operator.' Have one embedded story ready with the operator friction you hit and the baseline behind 40/63/23.

Pitch fix 3: close on a work question ('Which workstream would I start in, and how much of the week is at the customer site?'), not on pace. Keep pace and level for the hiring manager as 'what does a hard week look like for an EPM'. Add one line for Talor: targeting a lead-level seat, range once level is known, no number.
Pitch fix 4: be ready to say where ARCS stops and a customer deployment begins, and offer a carve-out for it. Disclose early; it is the PIIA point (invention-assignment agreement) in advance.

Resume decisions applied 2026-10-05: cut 'seven-figure' and 'Client sprints now run on ARCS'; summary now leads with the Squat NY embedded engagement (behavioral health client); dropped the PR-count headline; Grayscale scoped to the investor-facing surfaces with the $7B described as the platform's portfolio. 'Two decades' kept: career started 2006. Refuted by the verifier: 'pace question comes too early in the pitch'.

Challenge-site finding (2026-10-05, post-call prep): the coding challenge at challenge.percepta.ai (xterm.js terminal over a WebSocket, hosted on Railway) has a sandbox boundary that `cd /` escapes to the host filesystem; sibling session directories for other candidates (player_xxxxx) are visible from there. File-level Unix permissions held: entering those directories returned permission denied. Best guess: ~70/30 unintentional config bug over a deliberate behavioral test, reasoned from the fact that the deeper access-control layer worked correctly (a staged honeypot would either gate nothing or plant something to find) and the stack reads as fast-build, not an elaborate instrument. Action taken: stopped at permission-denied, did not explore further. Holding a disclosure note (routed through Talor, not sent yet) until after talking to him live.

Why it does not change the move either way: if deliberate, minimal-test-then-report is the intended answer; if a real bug, it is the responsible thing to do regardless. Percepta's own posted values give direct cover: 'Heart in the game... internally, that means fixing badness when you find it' and 'Make the call... make the decision and make the phone call.' Report plainly; do not over-narrate the test-or-not question in the note itself.
